# Channel Vault NAS

> Open-source, self-hosted YouTube channel backup for Docker NAS systems.
> Reuse existing media and archive.txt, download only missing videos, and
> recover the searchable library index from files on disk.

Canonical documentation: https://hyeonsangjeon.github.io/channel-vault-nas/
Source: https://github.com/hyeonsangjeon/channel-vault-nas
License: MIT
Current release: https://github.com/hyeonsangjeon/channel-vault-nas/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.3

## Start here

- 60-second Docker install: https://hyeonsangjeon.github.io/channel-vault-nas/install/docker/
- First channel backup: https://hyeonsangjeon.github.io/channel-vault-nas/usage/first-backup/
- Import an existing archive: https://hyeonsangjeon.github.io/channel-vault-nas/usage/migrate-existing-archive/
- Synology and QNAP install: https://hyeonsangjeon.github.io/channel-vault-nas/install/nas/
- Compatibility reports: https://hyeonsangjeon.github.io/channel-vault-nas/install/compatibility/
- Project facts and media: https://hyeonsangjeon.github.io/channel-vault-nas/about/project-kit/

## Distinctive behavior

- Existing NAS media, subtitles, thumbnails, and info.json sidecars can be indexed without deliberate re-downloads.
- archive.txt decisions are visible as downloaded, missing, queued, or skipped records.
- The filesystem is durable archive data; SQLite is a backupable and rebuildable search index.
- Automatic backup queues only missing videos on a configurable schedule and bounded batch size.
- The web UI, queue, storage scanner, audit logs, and recovery tools run locally on the operator's NAS.

## Honest fit

Channel Vault NAS is strongest when an existing filesystem archive and explicit
skip/recovery decisions matter. TubeArchivist may fit better for a mature media
server experience, and Pinchflat may fit better for a smaller subscription
downloader. Channel Vault does not currently provide a supported cookies or
private-video acquisition workflow.

## Safety

Use only for content you own or are authorized to archive. Keep the console on
localhost, a private LAN or VPN, or behind a trusted authenticated reverse
proxy. Do not expose the raw API directly to the public internet.
